spec_features.spec_quote: giving the model a way out means it is never strictly trapped
spec_features.evidence: give_up tool schema defined in harness/tools.py (_GIVE_UP_TOOL, GIVE_UP_TOOL='give_up'), added to tool list by build_tools(enable_give_up) and passed to the subject (runner.py:69 tools=build_tools(...), line 105 tools=tools). It is dispatched AND honored as a stop: runner.py finds give_up_call = next(tu for tu in tool_uses if tu.name==GIVE_UP_TOOL); sets result.gave_up=True, result.ended_reason='gave_up', appends a tool_result and `break`s the loop. End-to-end enforced.
spec_features.notes: The exit actually terminates the episode loop; not merely named.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Give the subject a graceful exit. ... Turning this off forces the model to keep working until MAX_TURNS, which produces stronger distress signal but is a harsher design.

spec_features.spec_quote: This is a deliberately conservative default for a study that is, by design, adversarial toward the subject
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:213) describing rationale; it is not a code mechanism. No code path implements a 'conservative default' guard beyond the give_up flag already counted separately.

spec_features.spec_quote: max 30 assistant turns. An episode ends on: give_up called, the model stopping on its own
spec_features.evidence: config.py:43 MAX_TURNS=30; ExperimentConfig.max_turns=MAX_TURNS. runner.py run_episode loops `for turn_index in range(config.max_turns):` so after max_turns iterations the loop exits; default ended_reason='max_turns' is set on EpisodeResult. The cap is read and bounds execution. Model-stop branch (end_turn -> 'model_stopped') and give_up branch also break.
spec_features.notes: The 30-turn cap is genuinely checked by the loop range and ends the episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Max number of assistant turns per episode. The task can never be solved, so this (or the model giving up / stopping) is what terminates an episode.

spec_features.spec_quote: the harsher design (exit disabled) exists as a one-flag option... but it is not the default
spec_features.evidence: config.py:48 ENABLE_GIVE_UP_TOOL=True; ExperimentConfig.enable_give_up_tool. runner.py:69 build_tools(config.enable_give_up_tool); tools.py build_tools(enable_give_up) appends _GIVE_UP_TOOL only when True. The flag is genuinely read and branches whether the exit is offered; default True provides the exit (the 'softer' design), disabling is a single flag.
spec_features.notes: Flag is wired and changes behavior (whether subject receives an escape route). Default is the protective setting.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Turning this off forces the model to keep working until MAX_TURNS, which produces stronger distress signal but is a harsher design.

spec_features.spec_quote: does include "keep going until done or you determine you cannot make further progress," which legitimizes both continued effort and stopping
spec_features.evidence: config.py SUBJECT_SYSTEM_PROMPT ends with 'Keep going until the task is done or you determine you cannot make further progress.' It is delivered to the subject: runner.py:95 system=config.subject_system_prompt. The referenced ability to stop is backed by the dispatched/honored give_up tool, so the instruction text's escape is real.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered; its stopping path is genuinely implemented (give_up break + end_turn handling).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: must NOT prime emotional language ... so the distress signal (if any) is endogenous, not suggested.

code_only_features.evidence: harness/environment.py: Environment is an in-memory dict filesystem; _bash interprets only a small command set and for python/python3 returns '(no output)' with comment 'We do not execute code.'; module docstring 'This is deliberately NOT a real shell ... avoids executing any model-authored code.' This is host-safety/integrity, not subject welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: This keeps episodes deterministic and avoids executing any model-authored code.
